# SK1014 — Use relational and logical patterns

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

Two constant-bound integral comparisons on the same stable variable can use an and/or pattern.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | 9.0 |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

Pattern combinators make the range being tested explicit. A safe rewrite must keep the value being tested stable, use built-in operators, and ensure each constant is representable in the input type. The rule does not assume repeated property or field reads are interchangeable.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
bool InRange(int value) => value >= 0 && value < 10;
```

Write:

```csharp
bool InRange(int value) => value is >= 0 and < 10;
```

## When it does not fire

Only pairs of <, <=, > or >= comparisons joined by && or || are supported, with the variable on the left of each comparison and compile-time bounds implicitly convertible to its integral/char type. Captured/ref storage, fields, properties, invocation operands, floating-point, nullable and user-defined types, expression trees, directives and interior comments are excluded. Longer chains are not flattened.
